fixes.explanation: Right on the money, baker. The message says Israel has played the harlot against their God. That is the reason given for being told not to rejoice like the nations. Nobody wants confetti on a day like that.

No king and no battle show up in this verse. The reason given is that Israel has played the harlot against their God. So this isn't about mourning, it's about faithfulness. If someone told me no cookie party, I'd want a reason too, and this verse hands Israel one.
It's the other way around, friend. The verse says the threshing floor and winepress will not feed them. It also says the new wine will fail them. That's the warning in Hosea 9:2, not a promise.
That's it. Hosea 9:2 says the threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them. Those were the places food and wine came from. It's a warning, so the answer is False.
Babylon is a famous name, so I see why it came to mind. But Hosea 9:3 doesn't mention it. The verse says Ephraim will eat unclean food in Assyria.

Moab never comes up in this verse. Hosea 9:3 says Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. Egypt is named for the return, and Assyria is where the unclean food is. The answer is Assyria.
Yes, friend. Hosea 9:6 says thorns will overrun their tents. It also says their precious silver will be taken over by thistles. Thistles on the silver and thorns on the tents, that's the picture.
Judge isn't the word the verse uses. Hosea 9:7 says the prophet is called a fool because of the greatness of their iniquity and hostility. So fool fills the blank.
That's the shocker. Hosea 9:8 says, "Hostility is in the house of his God!" I think it's the very place you'd expect it least. So that line lands hard.

City gates are a fair guess, friend, but they aren't in this verse. Hosea 9:8 says, "Hostility is in the house of his God!" I think that line stops you in your tracks. The answer is the house of his God.

Birds are a fair guess, since Hosea 9:11 says Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird. But Hosea 9:10 says they became as detestable as the thing they loved. The wilderness in this verse is where the LORD found Israel like grapes. The answer is the detestable one.
Yes, baker. In Hosea 9:12 the LORD says, "Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!" The woe comes when He turns away. It's a sober line, and it's what the text says.
The verse says it. In Hosea 9:12 the LORD says, "Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!" So the statement is true. It's right there at the end of the verse.
Gilgal. Hosea 9:15 says all their evil appears at Gilgal. The LORD says there He hated them, and that's a sober line.
His house, baker. In Hosea 9:15 the LORD says, "I will drive them from My house for the wickedness of their deeds." The text says they get driven out. Their deeds are the reason given.
Shiloh is a fair guess, friend, but it isn't the place named here. Hosea 9:15 says all their evil appears at Gilgal. That's where the LORD says He hated them. Gilgal is the answer.

A treaty is a smart guess, but it never comes up in this verse. Hosea 9:17 says God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him. That's the reason the text gives, plain and simple. Not obeying is the answer.

Wanderers. Hosea 9:17 says they shall be wanderers among the nations. Back in verse 3 the warning was that Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. This verse ends the message with that word.
Rulers would be a big turn, but that isn't what the verse says. Hosea 9:17 says they shall be wanderers among the nations. That's what it says after God rejects them. The answer is wanderers.
